claims.statement: Signatures are keyed by doc id and checked per actor; an empty signer (legacy save) skips the per-actor dimension, and a human menu click degrades to any-signer with the receipt saying so.
The gate checks exactly four dimensions — coverage, freshness, forgetting and per-actor — and refuses with `read_gate_missing`, `read_gate_stale`, `read_gate_forgotten` and `read_gate_other_actor`.
The forgetting window is `readGate.window` (default 80 dispatches); a version check at the same version never extends it, because only a body read resets the distance.

A `ver` is the first six hex digits of the page body hash, so it detects change but proves nothing about integrity, and it lives in one ledger file — never in the page body, which keeps exactly one home.

Amendments and both push-back routes advance `rev` and zero the signatures in the same transaction, so the next sweep reports missing coverage rather than a stale signature — a signature older than the new rev is not a reachable state.
An unreadable page — missing path, moved file, body contradicting the index — is a stop-and-report, never a licence to proceed from memory or from a single grep hit.
